correctness.rationale: The exact second-moment recursion is derived by conditioning on all four sign/refresh branches. The resulting cubic has \(P(1)=\alpha[2+\alpha-(1+4h^2)\alpha^2]/4\). The complete cubic Jury criterion is checked analytically: \(|c_3|<1\), the \(-1\) condition, and the reduced Schur condition \(J>0\) are all proved strict throughout the proposed interval. Equality produces eigenvalue \(1\), and larger positive steps violate the necessary \(P(1)>0\) condition.

value.rationale: The source method specifically uses rare snapshot refreshes to trade full-gradient cost against variance control. The natural \(n=2\), \(p=1/n\) model preserves that mechanism and yields a nontrivial exact stability loss as curvature heterogeneity grows. The result also shows that component-gradient noninterpolation does not move this boundary because its offset cancels exactly. These are directly interpretable algorithmic facts and provide a sharp benchmark beyond the general sufficient \(\eta\le1/(6L)\) theory.
